==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|physickal||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-}}
{{ety|en|:bor|la-lat:physicālis}}
{{bor+|en|la-lat|physicālis}}, from {{der|en|la|physica||study of nature}}, from {{der|en|grc|φυσική}}, feminine singular of {{m|grc|φυσικός||natural; physical}}, from {{m|grc|φύσις||origin, birth; nature, quality; form, shape; type, kind}}, from {{m|grc|φῠ́ω||grow}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-||to appear, become, rise up}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈfɪz.ɪ.kəl/|[ˈfɪz.ɪ.kəl]|~|[ˈfɪz.ɪ.kl̩]|a=RP,GA,CA,AU}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-physical.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|phys|ic|al}}
* {{rhyme|en|ɪzɪkəl|s=3}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# {{n-g|Of medicine.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} Pertaining to the field of [[medicine]]; [[medical]]. {{defdate|15th–19th c.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} That practises medicine; pertaining to [[doctor]]s, [[physicianly]]. {{defdate|18th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Wollstonecraft Mary|passage=Her father was thrown from his horse, when his blood was in a very inflammatory state, and the bruises were very dangerous; his recovery was not expected by the '''physical''' tribe.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} {{U|medicinal}}; good for the health, [[curative]], [[therapeutic]]. {{defdate|16th–19th c.}}
##* '''1579''', {{w|Thomas North}}, translating Pliny, ''Parallel Lives'':
##*: '''Phisicall''' {{transterm|grc|φαρμακώδεις}} herbes, as Helleborum, Lingewort, or Beares foote.
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius Caesar|act=II|scene=ii|passage=Is Brutus sick? and is it '''physical''' / To walk unbraced, and suck up the humours / Of the dank morning?}}
# {{n-g|Of matter and nature.}}
## {{sid|en|material}} Pertaining to the world as understood through the senses rather than the mind, having to do with the [[material]] world. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##: {{syn|en|''See'' [[Thesaurus:substantial]]}}
##: {{ux|en|It's not so much a '''physical''' place as a state of mind.}}
##* {{RQ:Mill Political Economy
|passage=Labour, then, in the '''physical''' world, is {{...}} employed in putting objects in motion.}}
##* {{RQ:Economist|title=No hiding place
|date=2013-05-25|volume=407|issue=8837| page=74| url=http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no| passage=In America alone, people spent $170 billion on “direct marketing”—junk mail of both the '''physical''' and electronic varieties—last year. Yet of those who received unsolicited adverts through the post, only 3% bought anything as a result.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025020559/https://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no|archivedate=25 October 2017}}
## In accordance with the laws of [[nature]]; now specifically, pertaining to [[physics]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|The substance has a number of interesting '''physical''' properties.}}
## Denoting a [[map]] showing natural features of the [[landscape]] (compare {{m|en|political}}). {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
# {{n-g|Of the human body.}}
## Having to do with the [[body]] as opposed to the mind; [[corporeal]],  [[bodily]]. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|Insults can hurt a lot more than '''physical''' injuries.}}
##: {{ux|en|Are you feeling any '''physical''' effects?}}
##* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|chapter=1|passage=A society sunk in ignorance, and ruled by mere '''physical''' force.}}
## {{1|sexual}}, [[carnal]]. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
##: {{coi|en|to [[get physical|get '''physical''']]}}
## Involving bodily [[force]] or [[contact]]; [[vigorous]], [[aggressive]]. {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|This team plays a very '''physical''' game, so watch out.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en
|date=December 1, 2017
|author=Tom Breihan
|title=Mad Max: Fury Road might already be the best action movie ever made
|work=w:The Onion AV Club
|url=https://www.avclub.com/mad-max-fury-road-might-already-be-the-best-action-mov-1820691831
|page=
|passage=Hardy is perfect. He’s '''physical''' and monosyllabic.
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307045929/https://www.avclub.com/mad-max-fury-road-might-already-be-the-best-action-mov-1820691831}}
# Of a piece of media, existing as a [[tangible]] object instead of being digital.
#: {{ux|en|There is just something so amazing about reading a '''physical''' book as compared to an [[e-book]].}}

====Antonyms====
* {{l|en|mental}}, {{l|en|psychical}}, {{l|en|psychological}}, {{l|en|spiritual}}; having to do with the mind or spirit (or both) viewed as distinct from body.
